structured.name: Burundi
structured.naturalResources: nickel, uranium, rare earth oxides, peat, cobalt, copper, platinum, vanadium, arable land, hydropower, niobium, tantalum, gold, tin, tungsten, kaolin, limestone

prose.hook: Landlocked in Central Africa between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Tanzania, Burundi straddles the crest of the Nile-Congo watershed. Its Kagera River, which drains into Lake Victoria, is counted as the most remote headstream of the White Nile. The country's resources include nickel, uranium, rare earth oxides, cobalt, gold, and tin, and it exports gold, coffee, tea, tin ores, and iron bars.
prose.physicalGeography: The terrain is hilly and mountainous, dropping to a plateau in the east with some plains. Burundi sits east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and west of Tanzania, landlocked with no sea access.
prose.climate: The climate is equatorial, shaped by a high plateau with considerable altitude variation from 772 to 2,670 meters above sea level. Average annual temperature shifts with altitude, ranging from about 23 to 17 degrees Celsius, and is generally moderate. Rainfall averages around 150 centimeters a year, split between two wet seasons (February to May and September to November) and two dry seasons (June to August and December to January), and the country is subject to flooding, landslides, and drought.
prose.economy: Burundi has a highly agrarian, low-income Sub-Saharan economy facing declining foreign assistance and increasing fiscal insolvency, compounded by a dense and still-growing population. The COVID-19 period weakened economic recovery and ended two years of deflation. Exports include gold, coffee, tea, tin ores, and iron bars, while industries center on light consumer goods such as sugar, shoes, soap, and beer, along with cement, assembly of imported components, public works construction, and fruit processing.
prose.peopleAndCulture: The population is overwhelmingly Christian, at 93.9 percent, split between Roman Catholic (58.6 percent) and Protestant (35.3 percent, including Adventist and other Protestant denominations), with a small Muslim minority of 3.4 percent. Ethnic groups include Hutu, Tutsi, Twa, and South Asian communities.
